selected_evidence.text: Atherosclerotic plaque accumulation in the coronary arteries is the leading cause of coronary heart disease, also known as coronary artery disease. Plaque causes coronary arteries to harden and narrow, potentially reducing or blocking blood flow to the heart muscle.

CDC directly states that coronary artery disease can weaken heart muscle over time and may lead to heart failure. The Causes section explains that atherosclerotic plaque narrows coronary arteries and may partially or completely obstruct blood flow.

selected_evidence.text: NHLBI identifies chronic damage or weakening of heart muscle as a major cause of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Reduced ventricular contractile capacity can impair cardiac pumping and lead to heart failure. The relationship is a supported causal pathway particularly for HFrEF and does not imply that all heart failure develops through the same mechanism.

selected_evidence.text: NIDDK states that hypertension can damage renal blood vessels and other components of the kidney filtering system. Damage to these structures can impair the kidneys' ability to remove waste and excess fluid. The page identifies high blood pressure as a common cause of chronic kidney disease.

selected_evidence.text: NIDDK identifies Hashimoto disease as the most common cause of hypothyroidism. The Hashimoto-specific passage explains that the immune system attacks the thyroid, the gland becomes inflamed, and it cannot produce sufficient thyroid hormones. This directly supports the narrower inflammation-to-reduced-hormone-production mechanism.

NIDDK explicitly states that autoimmune thyroid injury damages the gland and reduces its ability to produce sufficient thyroid hormones. It identifies hypothyroidism as a common consequence of Hashimoto disease and explains that many affected patients develop hypothyroidism as their disease progresses.
NIDDK states that Hashimoto's disease is the most common cause of hypothyroidism and describes autoimmune thyroid injury.

selected_evidence.text: NIDDK states that type 2 diabetes develops when the body has difficulty using insulin and the pancreas does not make enough insulin to maintain glucose balance. Insulin resistance contributes to hyperglycemia and type 2 diabetes in the context of inadequate insulin secretion.
NIDDK includes family history in its list of type 2 diabetes risk factors.
NIDDK lists overweight or obesity among circumstances associated with higher likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes.

Endotext describes insulin resistance in liver and muscle as an important pathogenic feature of type 2 diabetes; compensatory beta-cell secretion can initially maintain normal glucose, whereas inadequate beta-cell compensation permits hyperglycemia and progression to overt diabetes.

selected_evidence.text: Cigarette smoking promotes atherosclerotic plaque buildup by damaging cells lining blood vessels, increasing plaque accumulation, and contributing to arterial thickening and narrowing. The CDC explicitly identifies increased plaque buildup as an effect of smoking.

NHLBI identifies cigarette smoking as the most common cause of COPD in the United States and states that long-term tobacco smoke exposure damages the lungs and airways. The article separately describes thickened and inflamed airway walls in COPD.

NCI explains that chronic exposure to carcinogens in cigarette smoke produces genetic damage involved in multistep lung carcinogenesis. The article specifically identifies the association between cigarette smoking and DNA adduct formation in human lung tissue as evidence of tobacco-related genetic damage.
